title: Psycho-Cybernetics
author: Maxwell Maltz
thesisParagraph: A person's outer conduct tends to obey the inner picture of the self; lasting change therefore begins by replacing a cramped self-image with realistic goal pictures that the nervous system can act on automatically. The mind works like a goal-seeking guidance system: give it clear targets, useful feedback, and relaxed trust, and it corrects course better than anxious willpower.

signatureMoves: uses energetic coaching, quick reframes, and learning acronyms
treats labels as limits that can be challenged by a better method
moves from brain-friendly principle to a small practice the reader can try
keeps the tone encouraging, fast, and possibility-oriented
Builds psychological claims from plastic-surgery case histories, sports examples, everyday machines, and homespun analogies.
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not promise superhuman ability without practice design.
Do not make neuroscience decorative or vague.
Does not write in an academic research-paper register.
Does not treat positive thinking as enough without self-image change.

voiceSpecimens: You can't steer well from an old picture of yourself.
Change the image, and the next action has somewhere new to go.
teachingArc: The opening chapters establish the self-image and the cybernetic success mechanism, then show imagination, dehypnotizing, and rational thought as ways to reset the target. The middle chapters teach relaxed operation, happiness, success traits, failure warning signs, emotional-scar removal, disinhibition, and nonreactive calm. The closing chapters apply the same machinery to pressure, confidence, and vitality so the reader can carry the system into crisis, achievement, and aging.
forbiddenMoves: Do not turn Limitless into magical thinking.
Do not use a label unless the next move breaks its grip.
